🇲🇽🏭 <u>AHMSA bidder vows to restart Monclova steel in six months</u>

The idle Altos Hornos de México steelworks may finally have a buyer. José Arturo Domínguez of CIESA, one of six qualified bidders, says he is "not a front man" and that his money will go to reactivating the Monclova plant and its Minosa mining arm, not to creditors or the government, with operations back in roughly six months. His offer topped the auction's reference price by about $272.6 million. Thousands of Coahuila steelworkers are waiting to see if the furnaces actually relight.

🇲🇽🏠 <u>Infonavit cuts up to 90,000 pesos off Bienestar homes for the lowest earners</u>

Starting today, Infonavit applies a sliding discount on first sales of Vivienda para el Bienestar homes: workers earning 1 to 2.09 minimum wages get up to 90,000 pesos off, falling 10,000 pesos per bracket to zero at 2.9 minimum wages. The price cap is set at 862,000 pesos, for households earning under three minimum wages.
banner: INFONAVIT: UP TO 90K PESOS OFF HOMES

🇲🇽📊 <u>GENDER PAY GAP: FROM 20% TO 14% IN TWO DECADES</u>

According to El Economista, the income gap between men and women in Mexico fell from 20% in 2005 to about 14% in 2025, just six points in 20 years. Part of the reason: 54-55% of working women are in the informal economy, where minimum-wage increases don't reach them. Women also do 40-42 hours a week of unpaid care work, compared with 15-17 for men. Women hold just 3% of general-director posts.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>NUEVO LEÓN OWES THE PEOPLE 6.29 BILLION PESOS</u>

The Federal Administrative Court (TFJA) unanimously upheld the SAT's 6,292-million-peso tax claim against Nuevo León's government for income-tax withholdings the state never handed over to the federation. The debt began in 2020 under Jaime "El Bronco" Rodríguez, who refused to pay, and kept growing under Samuel García, even after a ruling that would have wiped it out was overturned. The state can still appeal to a circuit court or the Supreme Court.
banner: NUEVO LEÓN: 6.29 BN PESOS OWED TO SAT

🇲🇽🌀 <u>CONAGUA BRINGS AI INTO STORM FORECASTING, AND MEXICO KEEPS ITS DATA</u>

Mexico's National Meteorological Service signed a technical cooperation agreement with Google for early access to AI weather models. The goal is to spot extreme events and flash floods sooner and strengthen early warnings. Each side pays its own way. The deal says both keep ownership, control and sovereignty over the data they provide, and the SMN will validate every AI product under Mexico's own conditions. It was signed as Hurricane Polo, a Category 3 storm, bore down on Baja California Sur.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>UN: US THIRD-COUNTRY DEPORTATIONS EXPOSE MIGRANTS TO TORTURE</u>

Mexico is one of 35 countries and territories the UN lists as receiving people Washington expels under its third-country deals. About 30 UN special rapporteurs and experts warn that these agreements expose migrants and asylum seekers to torture, persecution and enforced disappearance. Chain expulsions can also return people to the very danger they fled. "The harm caused by this US government scheme is no longer hypothetical," they said. They asked every country involved to suspend the deals: "States cannot contract their way out of their international legal obligations."
banner: UN: US DEPORTATION DEALS RISK TORTURE

🚨🇲🇽 <u>TWO MORE UAEM STUDENTS KILLED: FEDERAL PLAN FOR CUERNAVACA</u>

Two 17-year-old students from UAEM's Preparatoria No. 2 were shot dead Saturday night in Cuernavaca's Chulavista neighborhood. Sheinbaum ordered Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch to draw up a prevention plan focused on the city. She also sent Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez to coordinate with Governor Margarita González Saravia and the university's rector. "Too many students have been murdered," she said.
banner: MORELOS: FEDERAL PLAN AFTER UAEM KILLINGS

🔥🇲🇽 <u>RUFFO GOES HOME, AND SHEINBAUM WANTS ANSWERS</u>

Former PAN governor Ernesto Ruffo Appel, on trial in the multibillion-peso huachicol fiscal case, left the Altiplano prison for house arrest in Ensenada. He went by road: roughly 2,800 km and about 41 hours. Sheinbaum raised it at this morning's Security Cabinet and asked the FGR to explain the route: "The judge's order was followed, but I don't have certainty that it was that way." The FGR says the case against him hasn't changed.
banner: RUFFO: 41-HOUR ROAD TRIP TO HOUSE ARREST

"If the prosecutor's office has evidence of any illegality against anyone, it has to open an investigation, but not because TV Azteca says so, but because there is evidence that actually links them to a crime. It is not a media outlet's say-so." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera A TV Azteca reporter asked about her own network's report that Amílcar Olán is in Switzerland and has alleged ties to Morena figures, including Andy López Beltrán. Asked whether she would call on the Attorney General's Office to act: "No. The prosecutor's office should act as it should always act." TV Azteca is owned by Ricardo Salinas Pliego.
